\label{ch:fa-legal-or-not}

\begin{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قانونی} (qânuni)}{قانونی (qânuni)}]{\fa{قانونی} (qânuni) — legal, lawful}

\label{lesson:FA-C405-qanuni}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to observe, then the Persian for to break.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قانونی}}
\textbf{\fa{قانونی}} (\emph{qânuni}) — \textquotedblleft{}legal, lawful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{کار} \fa{کاملا} \fa{قانونی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in kâr kâmelan qânuni ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is completely legal.
\end{quote}

\emph{Qânun} \textquotedblleft{}law\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{قانونی}} is \emph{qânun} \textquotedblleft{}law\textquotedblright{} with the Persian adjective suffix \emph{-i}. \emph{Qânun} comes from Arabic \emph{qānūn}, which was taken from Greek \emph{kanōn} \textquotedblleft{}rule, measuring rod\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qânuni}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qânuni}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{qânuni}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to observe, then the Persian for to break, then say \emph{qânuni} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{قانونی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Legal, lawful\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{غیرقانونی} (gheyr-e qânuni)}{غیرقانونی (gheyr-e qânuni)}]{\fa{غیرقانونی} (gheyr-e qânuni) — illegal}

\label{lesson:FA-C405-gheyr-e-qanuni}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to break, then the Persian for legal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{غیرقانونی}}
\textbf{\fa{غیرقانونی}} (\emph{gheyr-e qânuni}) — \textquotedblleft{}illegal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{فروش} \fa{این} \fa{دارو} \fa{غیرقانونی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{forush-e in dâru gheyr-e qânuni ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Selling this medicine is illegal.
\end{quote}

\emph{Gheyr} \textquotedblleft{}non-, other than\textquotedblright{} + \emph{qânuni}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{غیرقانونی}} joins \emph{gheyr}, from Arabic \emph{ghayr} \textquotedblleft{}other than\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), to \emph{qânuni} \textquotedblleft{}legal\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{qânun} \textquotedblleft{}law\textquotedblright{} (Arabic \emph{qānūn}, from Greek \emph{kanōn}).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gheyr-e qânuni}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{gheyr-e qânuni}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to break, then the Persian for legal, then say \emph{gheyr-e qânuni} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تخلف} (takhallof)}{تخلف (takhallof)}]{\fa{تخلف} (takhallof) — an offence, a violation}

\label{lesson:FA-C405-takhallof}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for legal, then the Persian for illegal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تخلف}}
\textbf{\fa{تخلف}} (\emph{takhallof}) — \textquotedblleft{}an offence, a violation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{کار} \fa{یک} \fa{تخلف} \fa{جدی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in kâr yek takhallof-e jeddi ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is a serious offence.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{takhallofât}. Lighter than a crime, such as traffic offences.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{تخلف}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{takhalluf}, a verbal noun usually explained as staying behind or failing to comply, from the same Arabic family as \emph{mokhâlef}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مجازات} (mojâzât)}{مجازات (mojâzât)}]{\fa{مجازات} (mojâzât) — a punishment, a penalty}

\label{lesson:FA-C405-mojazat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for illegal, then the Persian for an offence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مجازات}}
\textbf{\fa{مجازات}} (\emph{mojâzât}) — \textquotedblleft{}a punishment, a penalty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مجازات} \fa{دزدی} \fa{زندان} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mojâzât-e dozdi zendân ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The punishment for theft is prison.
\end{quote}

\emph{Mojâzât kardan} — to punish.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مجازات}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{mujāzāt} (EtymDB), a word usually glossed as requital, paying back a deed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مجوز} (mojavvez)}{مجوز (mojavvez)}]{\fa{مجوز} (mojavvez) — a permit, a licence}

\label{lesson:FA-C405-mojavvez}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an offence, then the Persian for a punishment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مجوز}}
\textbf{\fa{مجوز}} (\emph{mojavvez}) — \textquotedblleft{}a permit, a licence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برای} \fa{ساختن} \fa{خانه} \fa{به} \fa{مجوز} \fa{نیاز} \fa{داریم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{barâye sâkhtan-e khâne be mojavvez niyâz dârim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We need a permit to build a house.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{mojavvezhâ}. \emph{Mojavvez gereftan} — to get a permit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مجوز}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{mujawwiz} \textquotedblleft{}what permits, what allows\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
